title: Review: Control of gene expression: transcription factors and epigenetics; Principles of homeostasis and negative feedback; The cell cycle and mitosis
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: HO01#t3 term and clue written for the game; HO01#t4 term and clue written for the game; CD01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CD01a#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CD01a#N.6b, GR01b#N.4, HO01#N.4b, CD01a#N.8, GR01b#N.12, HO01#N.7c, CD01a#N.11, CD01a#N.4, CD01a#N.10. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Receptor
items.clue: Part of a control loop that detects the stimulus.

items.label: Effector
items.clue: Muscle or gland that makes the response in a control loop.

items.label: Cytokinesis
items.clue: Division of the cytoplasm, usually beginning during telophase

items.label: Interphase
items.clue: G1, S and G2 together: most of the cycle, and not a resting stage

questions.stem: Which statement describes a cell in G2 of the cell cycle?

options.text: It is resting after its DNA was replicated and makes few new proteins until mitosis begins.
It has twice as many chromosomes as in G1, since each one was copied in S phase.
It has replicated its DNA, and it is making proteins and ATP and copying its centrosome.
It is copying the centromere of each chromosome so that the copies can organize the spindle.

questions.explanation: G2 follows S phase, so the DNA is already replicated. In G2 the cell makes proteins, produces ATP in large quantities and replicates its centrosome, ready for mitosis.

questions.stem: Blood cells from people living in a city with high levels of particulate air pollution were compared with blood cells from people living in an area with clean air. The pattern of methyl tags on the DNA of several genes differed between the two groups, but the base sequences of those genes were the same. Which conclusion is best supported by these findings?

options.text: The two groups must have differed genetically before any exposure to pollution
Air pollution acted as a mutagen, changing the genes in the blood cells
Air pollution altered gene expression without altering genotype
The altered tags will be inherited by the children of the exposed people

questions.explanation: Altered methyl tags with an unchanged base sequence is an environmental effect on gene expression: the expression pattern changed while the genotype did not.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the feedback mechanisms that maintain an organism's internal environment?

options.text: They keep each internal condition at one exact value, which does not vary from moment to moment.
They act at the level of the whole organism, but not between molecules or within cells.
They respond to changes caused by the organism's own activity and to changes in its surroundings.
They are called negative when they harm the organism and positive when they help it.

questions.explanation: Feedback mechanisms respond to internal changes, such as heat produced by working muscles, and external changes, such as a fall in air temperature.

questions.stem: A body cell has 4 chromosomes. It is in anaphase of mitosis. What is moving towards each pole of the cell?

options.text: Two whole chromosomes, each still made of two joined chromatids
Four chromatids: one sister chromatid from each of the 4 chromosomes
One chromosome from each matching (homologous) pair, chromatids still joined
Half of the cell's DNA, which each new cell will replicate after division

questions.explanation: Every chromosome splits at its centromere, and one sister chromatid goes to each pole. Each pole gets a complete, identical set of 4.

questions.stem: Female honeybee larvae in a hive are genetically alike. Larvae fed only on royal jelly develop into fertile queens; larvae switched to a diet of worker jelly develop into smaller, sterile workers. Which explanation is consistent with the understanding of gene expression?

options.text: Larvae fed worker jelly lose the genes that are needed for queen development
The diet alters epigenetic tags, so the two castes express different sets of the same genes
Royal jelly contains a mutagen that alters the base sequence of the larva's growth genes
The diet cannot cause the difference, so the caste of each larva must be fixed at fertilisation

questions.stem: In a person whose pancreas does not release insulin, which prediction about blood glucose concentration after a meal containing carbohydrate is best supported?

options.text: It returns to the set point as fast as normal, as the body adjusts to meet its own need.
It rises and stays high longer than usual, as the response that lowers it is missing.
It stays at exactly the set point, as homeostasis keeps blood glucose at a fixed value.
It falls below the set point, as glucagon, which lowers blood glucose, is still released.

questions.stem: A population of a hypothetical freshwater plant reproduces only by fragmentation: pieces break off a parent plant and grow into new plants by mitosis. Which claim about the new plants is best supported?

options.text: They carry the same genetic information as the parent, except for any rare new mutations.
They can differ genetically from one another, as each mitotic division mixes up genes.
They may inherit features that the parent developed during its life, such as insect damage.
They each carry only part of the parent's genes, as each fragment receives only some.

questions.stem: A cell of an organism has 8 chromosomes before its DNA is replicated. How many chromosomes and how many DNA molecules are in its nucleus at metaphase of mitosis?

options.text: 16 chromosomes, 16 DNA molecules
8 chromosomes, 8 DNA molecules
16 chromosomes, 32 molecules of DNA
8 chromosomes, 16 DNA molecules

questions.explanation: Replication gives each of the 8 chromosomes two chromatids, each a DNA molecule: 16 DNA molecules. The chromatids stay joined until anaphase, so there are still 8 chromosomes.

questions.stem: A dividing cell is examined after its two new nuclei have formed. Many small vesicles are seen gathering and fusing in a line across the equator of the cell, midway between the nuclei. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: It is a plant cell: the vesicles are assembling sections of new membrane and cell wall to separate the daughter cells.
It is a plant cell: the vesicles mark the line along which the cell membrane will be pinched inwards to split the cytoplasm.
It is a plant cell: the vesicles carry enzymes that soften the existing wall so that it can grow inwards across the cell.
It is an animal cell: the vesicles are new organelles that have been made from scratch so that each daughter cell has a full set.
